record.original_question: For trees T and mappings f with parking sequence s, can one enumerate or otherwise analyze defective parking functions, meaning pairs (T, s) or (f, s) in which exactly k drivers fail to park successfully?

evidence.quote: (5) A refinement of parking functions can be obtained by studying what has been called defective parking functions or overflow, i.e., pairs (T, s) or (f, s), such that exactly k drivers are unsuccessful. Preliminary studies indicate that the approach presented is suitable to obtain results in this direction as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let n and m be positive integers with m ≤ n. Consider one of the following two combinatorial structures on the vertex set [n] = {1,2,…,n}:

(A) Tree model. T is a rooted labelled tree on [n] with edges oriented toward the root. Each non-root vertex is regarded as a parking space, and the unique outgoing edge from a vertex points to the next space a driver tries upon finding the current space occupied.

(B) Mapping model. f : [n] → [n] is an arbitrary function, encoded by its functional digraph whose vertices are parking spaces and whose edges v → f(v) indicate where a driver moves when the current space is occupied.

Parking process. There are m drivers, and a "parking sequence" s = (s_1, …, s_m) ∈ [n]^m specifies, for each driver i, the preferred initial vertex s_i. Drivers arrive one by one. Driver i first attempts to park at s_i; if that vertex is already occupied, the driver moves along the directed edge to the next vertex, and continues until either finding an empty vertex (in which case the driver parks there) or returning to a vertex already visited / reaching a dead end without finding an empty space (in which case the driver is unsuccessful and leaves).

Defective parking functions. For a fixed nonnegative integer k, call a pair (T, s) (in model A) or (f, s) (in model B) a k-defective parking function if exactly k of the m drivers fail to park successfully.

Problem. Develop an enumerative theory of k-defective parking functions in these two settings. Specifically:

1. Determine the number T_{n,m,k} of pairs (T, s), where T ranges over rooted labelled trees on [n] and s ∈ [n]^m, such that exactly k drivers are unsuccessful.

2. Determine the analogous number M_{n,m,k} of pairs (f, s) with f : [n] → [n] and s ∈ [n]^m, in which exactly k drivers are unsuccessful.

3. Derive generating-function identities for these quantities, and obtain exact closed-form and asymptotic expressions, including a description of any phase transition occurring near m ≈ n/2.
artifact.category_tag: Defective parking functions on trees and mappings
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a direction for further study: while defective (overflow) parking functions on a line have been enumerated (Cameron–Johannsen–Prellberg–Tetali, 2008) and parking functions on trees and mappings have been analyzed (e.g., Kuba and collaborators, 2015–2016), the enumeration and analytic-combinatorial treatment of k-defective parking functions in the tree and mapping settings has not been carried out in the literature found. It is listed as a preliminary/open direction in a recent survey on parking problems on random trees.

status_evidence.title: Counting Defective Parking Functions
status_evidence.snippet: If k drivers fail to park, we have a defective parking function of defect k. Enumeration on the line is solved.
status_evidence.claim: Defective parking functions are enumerated in the classical (line) case, but not for the tree/mapping generalization.

status_evidence.title: Parking functions for trees and mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the total number of tree and mapping parking functions and phase change at m=n/2; does not treat the defective/overflow refinement.
status_evidence.claim: The tree/mapping parking function framework exists but the k-defective refinement remains to be carried out.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: A refinement of parking functions can be obtained by studying defective parking functions or overflow ... Preliminary studies indicate that the approach is suitable to obtain results in this direction as well.
status_evidence.claim: The defective version on trees/mappings is identified as a future direction with only preliminary indications.
